physical.title: Jar in the Shape of a Fruit
physical.summary: This dark-brown glazed jar, with the heavy clay body and translucent glaze on the cover and the top just below it, has a rare shape of a fruit. It has a narrow foot with several moldings and incised wavy pattern immediately below the cover which is shaped in the form of a curling fruit stem that forms a handle. It is difficult to determine what type of fruit was meant, possibly a squash.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a printed silk yantra cloth with Khom-script magic diagrams, Buddha images, and Thai monastery inscription—a Thai ritual textile, not a ceramic; the "ceramic" category is wrong but the object itself clearly belongs to Thai Buddhist ritual culture.

physical.title: yantra
physical.summary: Blue Cloth Yantra. A blue silk cloth on which is printed a yantra or magic diagram. The rectangular diagram has five borders of text in Khom script. Inside these are smaller magic diagrams consisting of geometric shapes, Buddha images, an ogre-like deity (called Rahu) and magic symbols, within and around which are letters and numbers in Khom script. The Buddha images are labelled beneath them with their names in Thai script. Below the rectangular diagram are the name of the monastery and the province in Thai. Attached with metal studs to the lower left corner of the cloth is a machine-moulded diamond-shape plate of metal (the ‘nom oklao.’) The whole cloth is edged with red thread.
